'''Erica Jen''' (Chinese: 任峻瑞; Rén Jùnrùi; circa 1952 – November 12, 2023)<ref name=inmem/> was an American applied mathematician.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Schrecker|first=John|date=1979-08-12|title=On the Making of Modern China (Published 1979)|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1979/08/12/archives/on-the-making-of-modern-china-china-the-china-difference-china-the.html|access-date=2020-11-05|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jen|first1=Erica|last2=Srivastav|first2=R. P.|date=1981|title=Cubic splines and approximate solution of singular integral equations|url=https://www.ams.org/mcom/1981-37-156/S0025-5718-1981-0628705-4/|journal=Mathematics of Computation|language=en|volume=37|issue=156|pages=417–423|doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-1981-0628705-4|issn=0025-5718|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/robust-design-9780195165326?cc=id&lang=en&|title=Robust Design: A Repertoire of Biological, Ecological, and Engineering Case Studies|date=2005-03-24|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-516532-6|editor-last=Jen|editor-first=Erica|series=Santa Fe Institute Studies on the Sciences of Complexity|location=Oxford, New York}}</ref> She was a researcher at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], a faculty member at the [[University of Southern California]], and a scientific director and faculty member at the [[Santa Fe Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cellular Automation Offer New Outlook On Life, The Universe, and Everything|url=http://abel.harvard.edu/archive/118r_spring_05/docs/erikajen.pdf|website=abel.harvard.edu/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Erica Jen's research works {{!}} Los Alamos National Laboratory, NM (LANL) and other places|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Erica-Jen-2029321582|access-date=2020-11-05|website=ResearchGate|language=en}}</ref>

Jen's research focused on the mathematical analysis of chaotic and complex behavior.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Announcing the Rule 30 Prizes—Stephen Wolfram Writings|url=https://writings.stephenwolfram.com/2019/10/announcing-the-rule-30-prizes/|access-date=2020-11-05|website=writings.stephenwolfram.com|date=October 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Her research areas included singular integral equations for crack propagation, the mathematics of cellular automata (a class of dynamical systems that evolve according to simple local interaction rules), and mechanisms of robustness in natural and social systems.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Six Degrees|url=https://wwnorton.com/books/Six-Degrees|access-date=2020-11-06|website=wwnorton.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Jen was born in 1952 to [[Chih-Kung Jen]], a Chinese-born physicist who played a leading role in reestablishing scientific exchanges between the U.S. and China in the 1970s. After her junior year at [[Yale University]], Jen attended Beijing University for further education, becoming the first American national allowed to study in China since 1949 and the first foreigner since the Cultural Revolution.

After returning to the U.S., Jen obtained a Ph.D. in [[applied mathematics]] from [[Stony Brook University]] of the [[State University of New York]] and was the first postdoctoral fellow at the Center for Nonlinear Studies at Los Alamos National Laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Center for Nonlinear Studies|url=https://cnls.lanl.gov/External/History.php|access-date=2020-11-05|website=cnls.lanl.gov}}</ref>

==Career==
Jen served as a university scholar and assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University of Southern California]] from 1983 to 1986. In 1986, she became a staff member in the theoretical division and acting deputy director of the Center for Nonlinear Studies at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].

In 1995, Jen joined the [[Santa Fe Institute]], a leading interdisciplinary research center for the study of [[complex adaptive system]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=A Founding Program on Robustness of Social Processes|url=https://www.jsmf.org/grants/2002030/|website=www.jsmf.org}}</ref> She initially served as vice president for academic affairs and later as a research professor. Jen was the [[principal investigator]] for programs in evolutionary dynamics, social networks, and distributed learning.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Johnson|first=George|date=1997-05-06|title=Researchers on Complexity Ponder What It's All About (Published 1997)|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/05/06/science/researchers-on-complexity-ponder-what-it-s-all-about.html|access-date=2020-11-05|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> During her time at the Santa Fe Institute, Jen developed the program on the robustness of physical, biological, ecological, and social systems. After 2003, Jen served as external faculty, a science board member, and a science board fellow at the Santa Fe Institute. Jen was also an editor of Physica D: Nonlinearity.

She died on November 12, 2023.<ref name=inmem>{{cite web|url=https://www.santafe.edu/news-center/news/in-memoriam-erica-jen|title=In memoriam: Erica Jen|publisher=Santa Fe Institute|date=January 10, 2024|access-date=2024-06-29}}</ref>
